core_obligations: Reduce to locally bounded complexes of finite locally free modules by choosing an envelope, or alternatively use the splitting principle, so that only the P_p behave as if E and F were sums of line bundles (proof lines 9625-9634).

Prove the binomial identity for the formal objects P_p(S, f, epsilon) = sum_{s in S} epsilon(s) f(s)^p by reducing to the polynomial ring on the disjoint union S amalg S' and checking that each monomial f(s)^i f'(s')^j occurs with the same coefficient on both sides (proof lines 9637-9653).

Translate the formal identity back into geometry: c_1(E tensor F) = P_1(E tensor F) = r(F)c_1(E) + r(E)c_1(F) using r(E) = P_0(E), and 2c_2(E tensor F) = c_1(E tensor F)^2 - P_2(E tensor F), expanded and compared with the formula in the statement (proof lines 9654-9676).
proof_roadmap: Choose an envelope to reduce to finite locally free representatives and record that the vector bundle statements are the corresponding known results (proof lines 9625-9634).
Set up the formal P_p(S, f, epsilon) model and verify the binomial identity monomial by monomial in a polynomial ring (proof lines 9637-9653).
Read off c_1 and c_2 from P_1 and P_2 using the relation between the P_j and the c_i (proof lines 9654-9676).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes c_1, c_2 and the general Chern polynomial of a derived tensor product E tensor^L F of two perfect objects whose Chern classes are defined, together with the multiplicativity of the Chern character and the binomial formula P_p(E tensor^L F) = sum_{p_1+p_2=p} binom(p, p_1) P_{p_1}(E) P_{p_2}(F) (statement lines 9600-9622). The proof does not simply quote the vector bundle case: after an envelope reduces both objects to locally bounded complexes of finite locally free modules, the author sets up an abstract combinatorial model of a finite set S with a sign map and a function f into a commutative ring, defines P_p(S, f, epsilon) = sum_{s in S} epsilon(s) f(s)^p, and proves the binomial identity there by reducing to the polynomial ring on the disjoint union S amalg S' and comparing the coefficient of every monomial (proof lines 1024-1063 region, that is proof lines 9637-9653). The c_1 formula is then derived exactly from P_1 and r(E) = P_0(E), and the c_2 formula is checked by expanding P_2 in the same splitting-principle style (proof lines 9654-9676). Organising the computation through the polynomials P_p rather than through individual Chern classes is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
